title: uncle_gaming_pc_grave
display_title: My uncle sold my gaming PC while I was deployed, so I sold something of his
beats: My uncle (52M) sold my $2,400 gaming PC for $300 while I was deployed, and told me the garage 'needed the space.'
I'm 24, I built that PC part by part over three years of overtime shifts, and he knew it.
He said, 'It's just a computer, you'll build another one,' like that settled it.
So I went through his storage unit, the one I'd been paying half the rent on for two years as a favor.
Inside: his 1967 Mustang project car, eleven years of restoration, still up on blocks.
I didn't touch the car. I just canceled my half of the storage payment and mailed him the final bill.
Ninety days later, the facility auctioned the unit for nonpayment, Mustang included, for $1,100.
He called me screaming, and all I said was, 'It's just a car, you'll build another one.' Was I wrong?
